name: Robert E. Peary, The Polar Regions showing the Routes and Explorations of Robert E. Peary, U.S.N., from 1892 to 1906, in Nearest the Pole (New York, 1907)
note: 2729x2344. The first depiction of Crocker Land, on the foldout map in Peary's own account of the 1906 sledge journey: a crescent of hachured high ground at about 103 W, 82.9 N, concave to the north, its south shore - the side he saw it from, at Cape Thomas Hubbard - drawn as a dashed line, the north edge left to fade. Grosvenor's 1910 National Geographic map copies it. Chosen by Etienne, October 2026, over Grosvenor 1910 and Balch 1912.
polar_note: An equidistant polar sheet with the pole drawn on it at (1370, 75): meridians every 5 degrees of longitude are 5 degrees of angle apart about it, 60 W straight down (bottom-border labels 90 W at x 143, 60 W at x 1383, 30 W at x 2600), and parallels every degree are 142 px apart. Fitted by least squares on 26 meridian and 24 parallel crossings near Crocker Land (80-85 N, 90-120 W): RMS 1.8 px, about 1.4 km.
